items.title: flags(zsh): give --field-{context,match}-separator their argument in completions
items.body:
`crates/core/flags/complete/rg.zsh` declares `--field-context-separator` and `--field-match-separator` as bare switches, but both are value flags in the parser (`is_switch() -> false`, `doc_variable() -> Some("SEPARATOR")`; crates/core/flags/defs.rs:1863-1871 and :1971-1979 at the base commit). Because the spec has no `=`, zsh's `_arguments` never consumes the separator value — after `rg --field-match-separator ` the next word is completed as a positional/file argument instead of the option's value.

The fix gives both lines the same `[description]:separator` form used by the other value-taking flags in the file (e.g. `--context-separator` at :79). No option names change, so `ci/test-complete`, which strips everything after `=` when parsing specs (:59), compares the same set as before.

Verification boundary: this sandbox has no zsh I can execute (`bash -n`-style checks were also refused by the local permission layer), so the change was verified by line-for-line comparison against the existing value-flag specs in the same file and against the two flag definitions in `defs.rs`. I did not add or modify any other line.

Related: this completion file is hand-maintained (unlike the bash/fish/PowerShell ones, which are generated by `rg --generate`), which is how the drift in these two entries went unnoticed.

items.title: ignore: reject non-regular files as gitignore input
items.body:
Fixes #3569.

## Problem

`GitignoreBuilder::add` opens the ignore file and reads it line by line with no check of its type. A `.gitignore` that is a symlink to `/dev/zero` reads as one endless line and grows memory until the process dies; a FIFO blocks the read forever. Both can arrive in a checkout since git commits symlinks, and `add_parents` hits the same path for parent directories before `filter_entry` can skip them.

## Fix

After `File::open`, the opened file's metadata is checked and anything that is not a regular file is reported as an error. Checking the opened file rather than the path avoids a stat/open race, and symlinks to real files keep working since open follows them first.

## Tests

`crates/ignore/tests/gitignore_not_regular_file.rs`, following the per-issue test file convention: a directory and (on unix) a symlink to `/dev/null` are both rejected. The symlink test fails on unmodified code; the directory case already errored at read time but is covered for completeness. `cargo test -p ignore` passes 196 tests.

items.title: Unify flag metadata into a single validated source of truth
items.body:
Promote the FLAGS registry to a documented, validated single source of truth via a read-only RegistryView, and derive every flag-facing artifact from it: Bash, Zsh, Fish and PowerShell completions, the man page, and -h/--help output.

- Add RegistryView with registry-wide validation (duplicate/missing-field) and shared category/flag ordering.
- Replace the panicking custom-markup path with a fallible Markup_Renderer that centralizes roff hyphen escaping.
- Generate the Zsh completion's per-flag content from the registry (new !FLAGS! splice point) while keeping the hand-written scaffold and contextual grouping.
- Make value completion consistent across all four shells and complete negated names and aliases everywhere.
- Add a structured Consistency_Checker that reports all divergences; wire its real-registry test as the authoritative CI drift guard, replacing the loose zsh-only ci/test-complete.
- Formalize the --generate command contract and add integration tests.
- Implement all 25 design properties as proptest property tests plus example tests.

Spec: .kiro/specs/unified-flag-source

items.title: perf(searcher/mmap): advise sequential access for file-backed mmaps on Unix

labels.name: rollup
labels.description: A PR that has been merged with many others in a rollup.

items.body:
This applies `memmap2::Mmap::advise(Advice::Sequential)` after mapping a file on Unix. This is particularly important on macOS where mmap performance has historically been inconsistent (see #36). We also log `madvise` failures at debug level (including the path when available).

## Benchmark (macOS, 4GB file)
Command (as-run):

```sh
hyperfine --warmup 5 \
  'rg -a "foo" test_large_file || true' \
  './target/release/rg -a "foo" test_large_file --no-mmap || true' \
  './target/release/rg -a "foo" test_large_file --mmap || true'
```

Results:

- released `rg` (PATH), default behavior: 2.569 s ± 0.529 s
- local `./target/release/rg --no-mmap`: 2.548 s ± 0.315 s
- local `./target/release/rg --mmap`: 530.1 ms ± 362.8 ms

(So local `--mmap` is ~4.8× faster than local `--no-mmap` on this workload.)

## Safety / escape hatch
File-backed mmaps can SIGBUS if the underlying file is truncated while being read. Users can opt out with `--no-mmap` (already documented in the CAVEATS).

## Testing
- cargo fmt --all --check
- cargo test --workspace --features pcre2
- ci/test-complete
